validity.researcher_notes: SegmentName='Westbrook Xpress Project Phase 3' (operating, StartYear1=2021, LengthKnownKm already correctly 0.00), FERC Docket CP20-16 covers Phases II and III together. Downloaded and read the FERC Environmental Assessment (CP20-16-EA.pdf, 2020-04) with pdftotext: 'PNGTS states the purpose of Phase II and Phase III of the Westbrook XPress Project... is to increase the certificated capacity on PNGTS's wholly-owned Northern Facilities by about 81 MMcf/d and increase PNGTS's certificated capacity on the [Maritimes-jointly-owned] system... by about 50 MMcf/d,' and explicitly: 'There are no environmental impacts associated with Phase III of the Project; therefore, it will not be discussed further in this EA.' Phase II's own physical scope is a new compressor unit plus ~1,500 ft of 30-inch suction/discharge yard piping AT the existing Westbrook Compressor Station (Cumberland Co., Maine) -- station piping, not a mainline lateral -- and modifications at the existing Westbrook M&R station; no new mainline pipe or looping anywhere in Phase II or III. Independently, EIA's 'Today in Energy' (eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=50376, a different, non-regulatory federal source from the FERC docket) describes the same in-service event (2021-10-21) purely in terms of the new compressor station raising throughput -- 'The new Westbrook compressor station in Westbrook, Maine, will increase capacity on the co-operated Maritimes Northeast pipeline by 50 MMcf/d' -- with no pipe/looping mentioned. Two independent sources (FERC's own EA and EIA) agree this is a compression-and-M&R-station project with zero new mainline pipe, so a blank Diameter is the correct, confirmed value for this Phase-3-specific row, not an omission -- the wiki's '24-inches' describes the existing PNGTS/Maritimes mainline (elsewhere stated in the same EA as 30-inch, for what it's worth), not anything built by this project.
